Title: Dynamic Modeling of Microalgae Growth and Lipid Production under Transient Light and Nitrogen Conditions

Abstract: ABSTRACT: We developed a new dynamic model to characterize how light and nitrogen regulate the cellular processes of photosynthetic microalgae leading to transient changes in the production of neutral lipids, carbohydrates, and biomass. Our model recapitulated the versatile neutral lipid synthesis pathways via (i) carbon reuse from carbohydrate metabolism under nitrogen sufficiency and (ii) fixed carbon redirection under nitrogen depletion. We also characterized the effects of light adaptation, light inhibition hysteresis, and nitrogen limitation on photosynthetic carbon fixation. Model: Dynamic microalgae growth and lipid production model
Laws:
(9) [constitutive] Light absorbance per unit length is computed from chlorophyll carbon and the remaining biomass carbon using their optical cross sections.
(10) [constitutive] The reactor-average instantaneous light intensity is obtained by spatially averaging the attenuated light profile along the optical path.
(11) [constitutive] The reference average light intensity is calculated by averaging the unattenuated source-light profile along the optical path.
(12) [constitutive] Photosynthesis per unit functional biomass follows a Steele-type light response with light limitation and inhibition, scaled by the ratio of total to functional biomass.
(13) [constitutive] The light saturation intensity is set by maximum fixation capacity relative to chlorophyll-associated conversion of light energy into fixed carbon.
(14) [constitutive] The effective carbon yield on light energy decreases exponentially with reference average irradiance.
(15) [constitutive] The fraction of carbon redirected from carbohydrate toward neutral-lipid accumulation is highest at low nitrate and decreases as nitrate increases.
(16) [constitutive] The Chl-a degradation rate increases with reference light intensity and nitrogen starvation through error-function responses.
(17) [constitutive] The nitrate uptake rate per unit functional biomass scales with extracellular nitrate normalized by its initial value and is regulated by the current quota relative to its minimum and maximum quotas.
(18) [definition] The total nitrogen quota is calculated as cellular nitrogen concentration divided by total biomass carbon concentration.
(1) [balance] The functional biomass balance adds photosynthetic carbon allocated to functional biomass and subtracts functional biomass degradation.
(2) [balance] The carbohydrate balance adds the photosynthetic allocation to carbohydrates and subtracts respiration, nitrogen-associated losses, and carbon redirected to neutral lipids.
(3) [balance] The neutral-lipid balance accumulates lipids produced through nitrogen-associated synthesis and redirection of carbohydrate carbon.
(4) [balance] The Chl-a balance adds light-dependent synthesis associated with nitrogen uptake and subtracts Chl-a degradation.
(5) [balance] The reactor nitrate balance decreases nitrate concentration according to uptake by functional biomass.
(6) [balance] The cellular nitrogen balance increases intracellular nitrogen through nitrate uptake by functional biomass.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- X_{cd}: Concentration of functional biomass (algal biomass excluding carbohydrates and neutral lipids) as C
- X_{carb}: Concentration of carbohydrates as C
- X_{nl}: Concentration of neutral lipids as C
- X_{chl}: Concentration of Chl-a as C
- S_{NO3}: Concentration of nitrate as N in the reactor
- X_{N}: Concentration of cellular nitrogen as N

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- X_{C}: Total carbon concentration of the biomass
- S_{NO3_0}: Reference (initial) extracellular nitrate concentration in the uptake-rate expression

Model-wide assumptions:
- Optical cross‑section parameters a and b are taken as constant regardless of cultivation conditions.
- The composition of functional biomass is fixed to CH1.8O0.5N0.2.
- Nitrate uptake is assumed to equal the nitrate removed from the medium.

answer.description: The model predicts transient changes in functional biomass, carbohydrates, neutral lipids, chlorophyll, extracellular nitrate, and cellular nitrogen in Dunaliella viridis under varying light and nitrogen conditions. It couples light attenuation and light-regulated photosynthesis with nitrogen-dependent carbon allocation and quota-regulated nitrate uptake, using dynamic balances for the cellular components and reactor nitrate.
